name: subject-b-final-post-repair-v209
scope: post-repair audit of Subject B final-practice sustained-trace selection

reference_policy.use: attached FE references remain calibration-only for scope, terminology, difficulty and exam-style fidelity; proprietary wording is not copied
reference_policy.note: The sustained-trace classification and floor are FE QUEST internal quality controls, not an official IPA composition ratio.

post_repair_assessment.reasoning: The repair only replaces an algorithm item with an unused high-trace item of the same domain and level. It ranks replacement candidates by exposure before format load and prefers replacing more-seen low-trace victims. The readiness floor intentionally outranks global exposure fairness only when fewer than four sustained-trace items would otherwise be present.

low.evidence: Only 12 of 40 final algorithm items are in the sustained-trace class; the class is skewed toward applied items (3 standard / 9 applied), and the default object-oriented/standard and bit-string/applied domain-level slots have no compatible high-trace candidate.
low.impact: The floor is currently robust, but long-term repeated use can place more exposure pressure on a relatively small set of trace-heavy items than on the rest of the 40-item pool.
low.action: Do not change v209. Audit whether a small content-density expansion should add high-trace candidates to underrepresented domain/level cells before raising the floor or changing question counts.

decision.next_scope: Subject B final algorithm content-density expansion audit, prioritizing underrepresented domain/level cells without changing the final-session contract
